purpose: Canonical Coachi TikTok/Instagram slideshow format catalog. Copy structure only; all public copy must be original Coachi runner language.

default_slide_structure.purpose: Make the runner feel the exact problem immediately.
Name the behavior that creates the pain.
Add context that makes the correction believable.
Give the runner a simple rule they can use.
Connect the problem to Coachi only if it feels like the natural next step.
Ask for a save, follow, comment, or soft Coachi trial.

production_rules: Slides 1-5 teach before Coachi is mentioned.
Slide 6 may mention Coachi once when the problem fits live guidance, zone control, voice coaching, or Coachi Score.
Slide 7 uses a soft CTA, never a hard sales push.
Use one visual world and one lighting family per deck.
Use Images 2.0 for slide 1 only; use library/branded assets for the rest.
Keep hook text under 10 words unless a list format truly needs the number.

formats.pacing_notes: Fast list energy, but avoid stuffing five tiny tips into the deck. Use three memorable mistakes and one practical rule.
formats.visual_style_notes: High-contrast runner visuals, real training moments, no medical charts or watch close-ups.
formats.cta_style: Save this before your next run.

formats.hook_pattern: Your easy runs are probably too hard
formats.pacing_notes: Start with ego/pacing pain, then make slowing down feel useful rather than embarrassing.
formats.visual_style_notes: Calm road or forest route, steady effort, controlled breathing, no race visuals.
formats.cta_style: Save this for your next easy run.

formats.hook_pattern: Nobody talks about how slow Zone 2 feels
formats.pacing_notes: Use reassurance first, then explain context like heat, hills, and walking without sounding clinical.
formats.visual_style_notes: Quiet neighborhood or park path, soft light, calm confusion turning into control.

formats.pacing_notes: Reassure before instructing. The runner should feel less judged after every slide.
formats.visual_style_notes: Approachable park or city route, clean negative space, human not elite-athlete energy.
formats.cta_style: Your next run should feel controlled.

formats.hook_pattern: This is why your running stopped improving
formats.pacing_notes: Avoid blame. Show how too many medium-hard runs flatten progress.
formats.visual_style_notes: Repeating route, tired-but-real runner, muted training-day light.
formats.cta_style: Save this if every run feels medium-hard.

formats.hook_pattern: Most runners train like every run is a test
formats.pacing_notes: Contrarian but supportive. Make restraint feel athletic.
formats.visual_style_notes: During-workout steady movement, restrained effort, no finish-line or sprint imagery.
formats.cta_style: Try Coachi if you always run too fast.

formats.pacing_notes: Explain context without medical claims. Keep it practical: heat, hills, sleep, stress, effort.
formats.visual_style_notes: Real route context that explains effort; avoid medical visuals or device UI close-ups.
formats.cta_style: Save this before judging one run.

formats.format_name: Things I Wish I Knew Running
formats.hook_pattern: {count} things I wish I knew before running
formats.pacing_notes: Founder-led and humble. Use lessons, not commandments.
formats.visual_style_notes: Warm, human, post-workout or during-workout moments; avoid polished ad poses.
